title: Atoms are almost entirely empty space
body: Nearly all of an atom’s mass sits in its nucleus, yet the nucleus is tiny: the whole atom is roughly 27,000 (uranium) to 60,000 (hydrogen) times wider. If a nucleus were a marble, the atom’s electron cloud would stretch for hundreds of metres. So why don’t you sink through your chair? The electrons in its atoms and in yours repel each other, and quantum rules stop electrons from crowding into the same states.

slides.heading: How many times wider the atom is than its nucleus
slides.note: Whole-atom diameter divided by nuclear diameter; the exact figures are 60,250 and 26,634

slides.question: If atoms are mostly empty space, why don’t you sink through your chair?
options: The nuclei bump into each other
Electrons repel and can’t share states
Air fills the gaps inside the atoms

slides.clue: The tiny, dense centre of an atom, holding nearly all of its mass
